Module 3 renal supplement composition tables (6-8) and modular supplement Table 9 did not extract.
Module 6 Concept 2 quotes 2.5 g/day salt for hypertension. This is a general figure. Confirm the paediatric value from the PRNT sodium paper before use.

CKJ 2026 Tips paper: calcium SDI (220 to 1300 mg) and phosphate SDI by age (120 to 1250 mg, 940 to 1250 mg at 11-17 y) are quoted in an earlier draft but are not in the paper text layer; they appear in a table image. Verify before use.
CKJ 2026 paper gives dialysate glucose energy as about 7 to 9 kcal/kg/day; the course gives 7 to 10. Use the paper value for the rules engine pending clinician sign-off.

use_rules: Start from SDI for the child's age and sex, not from a fixed restriction.
Poor growth: aim for the upper end of the energy range.
Persistently high urea: move toward the lower end of protein only after other causes are excluded (total intake, hydration, catabolism, dialysis adequacy) and growth is protected.
Stage 2-3: avoid routine protein restriction, aim within normal range.
Stage 4-5 not on dialysis: maintain age-appropriate protein, avoid unnecessary restriction.
Dialysis: add protein to replace losses (PD +0.15 to 0.3 g/kg/day; HD +0.1 g/kg/day).
PD: count dialysate glucose as 7-10 kcal/kg/day toward total energy.
Infant feeds may need fortification (not dilution) when fluid limits reduce volume.

nephrotic_syndrome.relapse_definition: Urine protein 3+ or more on dipstick, or spot UPCR of 2 mg/mg or more.
nephrotic_syndrome.remission_definition: Urine protein nil or trace for 3 consecutive days, oedema resolved, urine output at baseline, weight stable at pre-relapse dry weight.

acute_relapse.energy_carbohydrate: Adequate energy, limit simple sugars especially on steroids, favour complex carbohydrate.
acute_relapse.protein: Adequate age-appropriate high-quality protein. Avoid both protein loading and very low-protein diets.
acute_relapse.fat: Children over 2 y: healthy fats, limit saturated and trans fat. Children under 2 y: no fat restriction.
acute_relapse.sodium: No-added-salt or sodium-reduced diet during oedema or hypertension. Prioritise fresh food.
acute_relapse.fluid: Do not restrict automatically. Restrict only on nephrologist advice (severe oedema, significant hyponatraemia, oliguria).

complete_remission.sodium: Normal sodium diet. Avoid added salt and very salty snacks.
complete_remission.fat: Continue limiting saturated and trans fat, especially after repeated relapses or steroid exposure.

principles: Most children with CKD do not need potassium restriction. Restrict only with measured hyperkalaemia on trend.
Renal K excretion is not significantly impaired until GFR is below about 15-20 mL/min/1.73m2.
Confirm on serial measurements. Base changes on trends; diet takes 3-7 days to show full effect.

Exclude non-dietary causes first: ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, calcineurin inhibitors, NSAIDs, beta-blockers, trimethoprim, constipation, acidosis, low energy intake, haemolysed sample, transfusion, inadequate dialysis.
hidden_potassium_sources: Low-sodium salt substitutes (200-300 mg K per gram)
potassium.leaching: Double-boil cut tubers, pulses and vegetables. If a food cannot be leached and K is high, avoid it in hyperkalaemia.
potassium.binders_infants: SPS 0.9 g per 100 mL lowers K by about 25%. Starting dose 0.4-1.5 g/100 mL. Recheck electrolytes after starting.

principles: Restrict phosphate additives first, not protein. Do not remove natural protein sources by default.
Use phosphate-to-protein ratio: prefer egg white, fresh unprocessed chicken and fish. Limit processed meat and cheese.
Calcium carbonate with meals acts as a binder. Count dietary plus binder calcium together.
additive_foods_India: Ready-to-eat curries and khichdi, poha, upma mixes

frozen_ready_meat: Fresh unmarinated chicken, fish or mutton, marinated at home
instant_noodles_soup: Home poha, upma, khichdi, idli or dosa

restrict_when: Hypertension or pre-hypertension, or on antihypertensives
CKD stage 2-4 with BP above 50th centile
increase_when: Infants and toddlers with growth failure from sodium wasting
PD with large dialysate sodium losses
sodium.salt_conversion: 1 tsp salt is about 6 g NaCl = 2400 mg sodium = 104 mEq
sodium.salt_substitute_warning: Avoid potassium-based salt substitutes in children with impaired kidney function.
sodium.assessment: Use 24-h recall, FFQ, or 3-day diary. Do not use serum or urinary sodium to estimate intake. Additives can raise intake by up to 60%.

PD.potassium: Do not restrict routinely; may need supplements.

HD.fluid: Restrict to limit interdialytic weight gain.
HD.potassium: Restrict as needed; accumulates between sessions.
HD.sodium: Restrict; important for thirst and weight gain.
HD.water_soluble_vitamins: Supplement. IV iron usually needed with ESA.

dialysis.IDPN: Only for persistent protein-energy malnutrition despite optimised oral and enteral support.

growth_and_weight.metabolic_syndrome: Overweight or obesity plus 2 of: low HDL, high TG, high BP, high fasting glucose or known T2DM.
growth_and_weight.obesity_approach: Individualise energy. Improve diet quality. Limit sugary drinks and processed food. Avoid aggressive restriction. No anti-obesity drugs in CKD 2-5D or post-transplant.
growth_and_weight.dry_weight: Dialysis dry weight is the weight with excess fluid removed, normal BP, and no dehydration or overload.
growth_and_weight.mid_parental_height: Boys: (mother + 13 + father)/2. Girls: (mother + father - 13)/2. Target range plus or minus 8.5 cm.

food_composition_group_averages_per_100g.source: Course Module 0 Table 10 (IFCT 2017 group averages). Replace with item-level IFCT values in the food table.

homemade_feed_example.name: Rice-moong feed (course Module 3, Concept 6)
homemade_feed_example.note: Standardise the recipe. Recalculate for the child's CKD stage and protein allowance.

model_case_rules.poor_growth_CKD3: Raise energy toward upper SDI. Do not reduce protein. No K or P restriction without biochemical indication. Replace biscuits and chips with planned energy foods.
model_case_rules.hyperkalaemia_CKD4: Check trend and non-dietary causes. Remove concentrated K (coconut water). Spread K foods across the day. Use leaching. Treat constipation. Do not remove all fruit and vegetables.
model_case_rules.hyperphosphataemia_CKD5: Remove phosphate additives first. Teach label reading. Keep protein foods; review portions. Check binder timing.
model_case_rules.HD_teen: Plan meals around school and dialysis. Add dialysis protein. Restrict salty food and fluid. Involve the adolescent.
model_case_rules.PD_toddler: Count dialysate glucose. Raise protein for PD losses. Consider supplements or enteral feeding early when oral intake is inadequate.

common_pitfalls: Restricting protein because the child has CKD.
Starting K restriction without confirming need.
Focusing on phosphorus and ignoring additives.
Multiple simultaneous restrictions causing low energy intake.
Using oedematous weight instead of dry weight.
Giving nutrient numbers without food quantities.
Ignoring constipation, appetite and feeding difficulty.
Plans too complicated for the family.
Failing to reassess when labs, dialysis or growth change.

ckj_2026_tips.source: Polderman N, Shaw V et al. Clin Kidney J 2026;19(4):sfag046

pd_protein_losses_g_per_kg_day.note: range from infants to adolescents; individual losses vary

fibre_sdi_g_per_1000_kcal.note: PRNT SDI for fibre; plant-slant diets advised

calcium.total_intake_pct_of_sdi: 100 to 200 (includes breast milk, formula, food, calcium-based medication)
calcium.note: Restrict phosphate without cutting calcium: use non-dairy sources (plant milks, calcium-set tofu, fortified cereals); calcium supplements or high-calcium dialysate may be needed

phosphate_bioavailability_pct.additives: up to 100 (identify by phos on ingredient labels)

ckj_2026_tips.phosphate_binders: Taken with food or formula; whey-dominant or renal formulas have lower phosphate
potassium_stepwise: Correct non-dietary causes first (medications, acidosis, constipation as per course).
Restrict potassium additive foods and other sources with added potassium.
Replace high-potassium, low-value foods with lower-potassium alternatives.
Do not routinely exclude fruit, vegetables or whole grains; they carry fibre and nutrient value.
Limit animal protein while still meeting protein needs.
If dietary control is inadequate or hard to sustain, a potassium binder such as sodium zirconium cyclosilicate can be used.
ckj_2026_tips.fortification: Expressed breast milk can be fortified with infant formula powder to 13% to 20% (67 to 100 kcal/100 mL); whey-dominant formula preferred for lower phosphate and potassium
ckj_2026_tips.tube_feeding: Start early when weight centile falls or oral intake is inadequate; NGT as bridge to gastrostomy; plan gastrostomy in PD (peritonitis risk, prophylaxis)
ckj_2026_tips.energy: Energy SDI; upper end for poor growth; height age for poor linear growth
ckj_2026_tips.ultra_processed_foods: Limit UPFs (NOVA); about 80% of sodium intake in Western countries comes from processed and UPFs; avoid salt substitutes
ckj_2026_tips.micronutrients: Monitor vitamins and minerals; supplement only when clinically indicated; limit oxalate-rich foods where relevant
